question: What happens to red blood cells during a sickle cell crisis?

options.A: Cells swell and burst open prematurely
options.C: Cells lose all of their surface proteins
options.D: Cells shrink into tiny spherical shapes

explanation: You've got this! Abnormal hemoglobin S changes the shape of the red blood cells, making them hard and crescent-shaped when they drop off oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h1)

question: Why does pregnancy put a woman with sickle cell disease at higher risk for complications?

options.A: Hormones produced during pregnancy destroy normal red blood cells
options.B: The growing uterus completely stops blood flow to the lower extremities
options.C: Pregnancy causes blood volume to rise and the body to clot more easily
options.D: High iron demands in pregnancy cause all hemoglobin to turn into hemoglobin S

explanation: Great thinking! Because pregnancy naturally increases blood volume and clotting tendencies, blocked blood vessels become a bigger risk for these mums. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h1)

question: Which serious lung condition is a major emergency for a pregnant woman with sickle cell disease?
explanation: Spot on! Acute chest syndrome involves lung infection and tissue damage, bringing chest pain and fever that needs fast medical care. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h2)

question: Why might a baby born to a mother with sickle cell disease grow more slowly in the womb?

options.A: Excessive amounts of amniotic fluid crushing the developing baby
options.B: Direct genetic damage to the fetal brain by maternal white cells
options.C: Reduced oxygen and nutrient transfer through the placenta
options.D: Premature closure of the fetal heart valves during the second trimester

explanation: Well done! When sickle cells slow down blood flow in the placenta, the baby gets less oxygen and food, which can slow down growth. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h2)

question: How often should an antenatal clinic see a pregnant woman with sickle cell disease during her first two trimesters?
explanation: Spot on. High-risk pregnancies need close monitoring right from the start—usually every two weeks to catch any problems early. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h3)

question: What is the main reason a nurse schedules serial ultrasounds for a pregnant client with sickle cell disease?

options.A: To check if the maternal pelvis is widening properly
options.B: To measure the exact volume of maternal amniotic fluid daily
options.C: To determine the exact genetic subtype of the fetus
options.D: To monitor fetal growth and screen for fetal anemia

explanation: You're doing great! Regular scans help us check how well the baby is growing and keep an eye out for fetal anemia. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h3)

question: Why do doctors usually stop hydroxyurea when a woman with sickle cell disease becomes pregnant?

options.A: It can cause birth defects in the developing fetus
options.B: It neutralizes the effects of routine folic acid supplements
options.C: It makes the maternal blood pressure drop dangerously low
options.D: It completely stops the bone marrow from making any blood cells

explanation: Exactly right! Hydroxyurea can harm a developing baby, so it is paused during pregnancy to keep the little one safe. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h4)

question: Which medication do doctors commonly start early in pregnancy to help prevent pre-eclampsia in women with sickle cell disease?
explanation: Brilliant! Low-dose aspirin is a helpful tool started early on to protect the placenta and lower the risk of pre-eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h4)

question: What is a major benefit of using an epidural for pain relief during labor for a patient with sickle cell disease?

options.A: It completely cures the underlying genetic hemoglobin defect
options.B: It stops the placenta from aging too quickly
options.C: It replaces the need for continuous fetal heart monitoring
options.D: It reduces maternal stress and prevents acidosis caused by pain

explanation: You got it! Controlling pain stops the mum from stressing and breathing too fast, which helps prevent acid build-up that can trigger a crisis. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h5)

question: A woman with sickle cell disease is admitted in active labor. What is the most critical nursing action for her care?

options.A: Restricting oral fluid intake to prevent swelling
options.B: Encouraging unmedicated natural childbirth at home
options.D: Keeping the room temperature cold to prevent shivering

explanation: Spot on! Dehydration makes the blood thicker and can easily trigger a crisis, so keeping fluids flowing through an IV is an absolute must. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h5)

question: Why do doctors generally avoid estrogen-containing contraceptives for women with sickle cell disease after childbirth?

options.A: They immediately stop all breast milk production
options.B: They cause permanent changes in maternal voice pitch
options.C: They increase the risk of dangerous blood clots
options.D: They destroy the effectiveness of folic acid supplements

explanation: Correct! Estrogen raises clot risks, and since postpartum mums with sickle cell are already prone to clots, it's best to steer clear. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h6)

question: Which nursing care measure is especially important to prevent blood clots right after delivery for a patient with sickle cell disease?

options.A: Stopping all pain medications immediately after delivery
options.B: Restricting fluid intake to decrease postpartum swelling
options.C: Encouraging early mobilization and preventing blood clots
options.D: Applying ice packs to the abdomen to slow down blood flow

explanation: Wonderful! Getting the mum moving early after delivery is a fantastic way to keep her circulation healthy and ward off nasty blood clots. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h6)
